executive_brief: This project is a foundational Technical Constitution template designed to establish governance, coding standards, and quality gates for a software project. It defines a structural framework for implementing a Library-First architecture, CLI-driven interfaces, and a strict TDD-based testing discipline. The document serves as the supreme architectural authority to ensure consistency across development workflows and system evolution.

architectural_constraints: Library-First: Every feature must start as a standalone, self-contained, and independently testable library
CLI Interface: Mandatory text-in/text-out protocol (stdin/args to stdout, errors to stderr) supporting JSON and human-readable formats
TDD Mandatory: Strict Red-Green-Refactor cycle (Tests written -> User approved -> Tests fail -> Implementation)
Integration Testing: Mandatory for new library contracts, contract changes, inter-service communication, and shared schemas
Governance Supremacy: The Constitution supersedes all other practices; amendments require documentation, approval, and a migration plan

maturity_assessment: The project is currently in a template state, providing a robust structural skeleton but lacking concrete project-specific values. While the health index is high, the presence of a medium-severity gap regarding the absence of an 'Open Questions & Uncertainties' section indicates that the framework for tracking architectural ambiguity is not yet implemented. However, as a structural blueprint, it is READY for population and execution.
critical_dependencies: Logical dependency between TDD (PRIN-03) and Integration Testing (PRIN-04) for full quality gate coverage
Governance (GOV-01) as the primary enforcement mechanism for all core principles (PRIN-01, PRIN-02, PRIN-03)
Requirement for a [GUIDANCE_FILE] to provide runtime development instructions
